q: What must the Jury do with a design that does not conform to the mandatory requirements, instructions, or Conditions of the ADC?
o: Refer it to the IAPOA ADC Committee for a final ruling
Request the Competitor to revise and resubmit
Disqualify it
Award it a reduced honorarium
n: The Jury shall disqualify any design which does not conform to the mandatory requirements, instructions or Conditions for the ADC. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 6.11)

q: In a two-stage competition, when may the names of Competitors selected to proceed to the second stage be made public?
o: Only under exceptional conditions agreed on by the Jury before the launching of the ADC
Immediately after the first-stage results, as a matter of transparency
Never, under any circumstance
Only after the Owner obtains written consent from the IAPOA President
n: The names of those Competitors selected to proceed to the second stage of a two-stage competition shall be made public only under exceptional conditions to be agreed on by the Jury before the launching of the ADC. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 10.3)

q: What distinction must the ADC Conditions make regarding competitors' submissions?
o: A clear distinction between mandatory requirements and those which permit the competitor freedom of interpretation
A distinction between digital and physical submission formats
A distinction between local and foreign competitors
A distinction between individual and firm-based entries only
n: A clear distinction shall be made between the mandatory requirements of the Competition and those which permit the competitor freedom of interpretation, and all entries must be submitted in the manner prescribed in the Conditions. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 4.4)

q: May a member of the Jury take part in the competition or be commissioned for the prize-winning design?
o: Yes, if approved beforehand by the Owner
No — no member of the Jury may take part in the competition, directly or indirectly, nor be commissioned with work connected with the prize-winning design either directly or indirectly
Yes, but only in a limited (invitational) ADC
Yes, provided he abstains from voting on his own entry
n: No member of the Jury will be allowed to take part in the competition, either directly or indirectly, nor be commissioned with work connected with the prize-winning design either directly or indirectly. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 7.1)

q: What must the Owner do regarding registered Competitors and the IAPOA after the ADC results are known?
o: Publish the results only in the Official Gazette
Notify only the winning Competitor; the IAPOA need not be informed

Notify all registered Competitors in a timely manner of the date/place of the exhibition and the results, send them a copy of the Jury's report, similarly inform the IAPOA, and send photographs of the prize-winning designs to the IAPOA with an option for publication
Withhold notification until the exhibition closes
n: The Owner shall notify in a timely manner all registered Competitors of the date and place of the public exhibition and the results of the ADC, and send them a copy of the Jury's report. He shall similarly inform the IAPOA, and photographs of the prize-winning designs shall be sent to the IAPOA with an option for publication. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 12.2)

q: Who appoints and pays the Professional Advisor for an ADC, and who must approve this appointment?
o: Appointed and paid by the IAPOA directly; no approval needed
Appointed and paid by the Owner; approved by the IAPOA National Board of Directors (NBD) through its ADC Committee
Appointed by the competitors themselves; approved by the Owner
Appointed and paid by the Jury; approved by the Competition Secretariat
n: A Professional Advisor should be appointed and paid by the Owner and approved by the IAPOA National Board of Directors (NBD) through its ADC Committee. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 5.1)

q: For an Ideas Competition only, what limited prize arrangement is permitted?
o: Only in-kind prizes (no cash) may be given
It may be possible to remunerate only the first (1st) prize winner
Prize money must be split equally among all entrants
No prizes may be awarded at all
n: It is important for the Owner to allot adequate prize money to compensate all the Competitors for their work; however, for an Ideas Competition only, it may be possible to remunerate only the first (1st) prize winner. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 8.2)

q: Who are the sole arbiters at all stages of the ADC, up to the final prize-giving?
o: The Owner's board of directors
The Professional Advisor
The Jury members
The IAPOA ADC Committee
n: The Jury members are the sole arbiters at all stages, up to the final prize-giving. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 14.2)

q: When must the Jury for an ADC be set up, and where must the names of Jury members (including reserve members) be stated?
o: At the Professional Advisor's discretion; in the exhibition catalogue
Before the official announcement of the competition; in the Conditions
After the competition closes; in the Jury's final report
Only after the second stage begins; in a separate memorandum
n: The Jury shall be set up before the official announcement of the competition, and the names of the Jury and its reserve members shall be stated in the Conditions. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 6.1)

q: In a two-stage competition, what must be paid to Competitors selected to take part in the second stage, and what is its purpose?
o: A refund of their first-stage registration fee only
A reasonable honorarium, stated in the Conditions, in addition to the prizes awarded, intended to reimburse them for the additional work carried out in the second stage
A share of the Professional Advisor's fee
Nothing further beyond the eventual prize, since honoraria apply only to limited ADCs
n: In two-stage competitions, Competitors selected to take part in the second stage shall be paid a reasonable honorarium, stated in the Conditions, in addition to the prizes awarded, to reimburse them for the additional work carried out in the second stage. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 8.5)

q: Overall, what kind of subject matter does SPP Document 208 govern within the Philippine architecture profession's Standards of Professional Practice?
o: The scale of professional fees for design services generally
The continuing professional development (CPD) requirements for licensed architects
The licensure examination syllabus for aspiring architects
The conduct of Architectural Design Competitions (ADCs) — covering the Owner, Jury, Professional Advisor, Conditions, prizes, copyright, registration, insurance, exhibitions, and dispute resolution
n: SPP Document 208 (part of the 2010 Standards of Professional Practice) sets out the rules governing Architectural Design Competitions — the roles of the Owner, Jury, Professional Advisor, and IAPOA ADC Committee, the drawing up of Conditions, prizes and honoraria, copyright and ownership, registration of competitors, insurance, exhibitions, return of projects, and alternative dispute resolution. (Source: SPP Document 208 (2010 Standards of Professional Practice), generally)

q: Aside from not exceeding seven (7), what other numerical requirement applies to the composition of the Jury?
o: There is no other numerical requirement
It must be an even number to allow tie-breaking votes
It must be divisible by three
It must be an odd number
n: The Jury shall be composed of the smallest reasonable number of persons and in any event should be an odd number, not exceeding seven (7). (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 6.3)

q: SCENARIO: In a Project ADC, the first-prize amount is PHP 500,000. The Jury announces its award on January 15, and no design/build contract is signed with the Owner within the period specified in the Conditions. QUESTION: Under SPP Document 208, what compensation must the first-prize winner receive, and what is the deadline that triggers it?
o: A sum equal to 10% of the project cost, payable within three (3) months
No further compensation is due; the first prize is the Competitor's sole recourse

A further sum equal to PHP 500,000 (the amount of the first prize) if no contract is signed within twelve (12) months of the announcement of the Jury's award — i.e., by January 15 of the following year
Double the original prize, but only if no contract is signed within six (6) months
n: In Project ADCs, provisions shall be made in the Conditions for the first prize winner to receive compensation of a further sum equal to the amount of the first prize (here, another PHP 500,000) if no contract is signed within twelve (12) months of the announcement of the Jury's award. The Owner still does not acquire the right to carry out the project except with the Author's collaboration. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 8.8)
scenario: In a Project ADC, the first-prize amount is PHP 500,000. The Jury announces its award on January 15, and no design/build contract is signed with the Owner within the period specified in the Conditions.

q: Under SPP Document 208, who is responsible for drawing up the full Conditions of an Architectural Design Competition (ADC), including the program, submission instructions, site plans, entry forms, and official envelopes and labels?
o: The Professional Advisor
The Owner's legal counsel
The IAPOA ADC Committee
The Jury Chairman
n: The Conditions (program, submission instructions, site plans, entry forms, official envelopes/labels) are drawn up by the Professional Advisor. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 2.7)

q: What is essential regarding attendance at meetings of the Jury?
o: A quorum of half the Jurors suffices for any meeting
Reserve Jurors may substitute for absent Jurors without restriction
It is essential that all Jurors be present at all meetings of the Jury
Only the Chairman need attend every meeting
n: It is essential that all Jurors be present at all meetings of the Jury. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 6.6)

q: When may the first-prize design be used by the Owner, and what applies to any other submitted plan/design?
o: The Owner may use any design without commissioning the Author, provided royalties are paid

The first-prize design may be used only upon the Owner commissioning the Author to carry out the plan/design preparation for the project; no other plan/design may be used wholly or in part except by agreement with its Author
Only designs that placed in the top three may ever be used
Any entry, prize-winning or not, may be used freely by the Owner
n: The design awarded first prize can only be used by the Owner upon his commissioning the Author to carry out the plan/design preparation for the project. No other plan/design may be used wholly or in part by the Owner except by agreement with the Author concerned. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 9.2)

q: Before the Owner makes any official announcement of an ADC, what must the IAPOA (through the ADC Committee) send to the Owner?
o: A written approval of the draft Conditions, including the timetable, registration fee (when required), and Jury composition
A signed copy of the winning design's copyright waiver
A notarized surety bond covering all prize money
A list of pre-approved Competitors
n: The IAPOA, through the ADC Committee, must send the Owner a written approval of the draft Conditions, including the timetable, the ADC registration fee (when required), and the composition of the Jury, before any official announcement. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 3.1)

q: In a two-stage competition, who should judge both stages, and under what condition may a competition originally approved as single-stage proceed to a second stage?
o: Any available Jury; approval from the Owner alone suffices
The Professional Advisor selects a new Jury for the second stage

The same Jury should judge both stages; a single-stage competition may proceed to a second stage only with IAPOA approval of the Conditions and honoraria arrangements for the Competitors involved, over and above the original prize money
A different Jury for each stage; single-stage competitions may never add a second stage
n: In a two-stage competition, the same Jury should judge both stages. A competition approved as single-stage may proceed to a second stage only with IAPOA approval of the Conditions and of arrangements for payment of honoraria to the Competitors involved, over and above the original prize money; if a secondary competition takes place, the original Jury must be reappointed by the Owner. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 6.9)

q: What must Competitors do upon receiving details of an ADC, and what does this act imply?
o: Register with the IAPOA ADC Committee directly; this implies eligibility for the Jury
Submit a preliminary sketch to the Professional Advisor; this implies conditional participation
Pay the full registration fee to the Jury Chairman; this implies a binding contract for the project
Register with the Owner; registration implies acceptance of the Conditions of the ADC
n: As soon as they have received details of the ADC, all Competitors shall register with the Owner. Registration implies acceptance of the Conditions of the ADC. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 10.1)

q: For a National ADC, how must the ADC conditions and program of requirements be presented to competitors?
o: They must be identical for all competitors
They may be modified individually upon competitor request
They may vary depending on each competitor's qualifications
They are issued only to competitors reaching the second stage
n: The ADC conditions, including the program of requirements of a National ADC, shall be identical for all competitors. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 4.2)

q: What obligation does the Jury have regarding awards, and how must it use the prize funds?
o: The Jury must make awards, final and made public by a date agreed with the IAPOA, making full use of the amount set aside for prizes in the Conditions
The Jury must award only a single top prize regardless of the amount set aside
The Jury may decline to make any award if no entry is outstanding
The Jury may redirect unused prize money to the Professional Advisor's fee
n: The Jury must make awards. The awards shall be final and made public by a date agreed on with the IAPOA and stated in the Conditions; the Jury, when distributing the awards, shall make full use of the amount set aside for prizes in the ADC Conditions. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 6.12)

q: Who is responsible for insuring the Competitors' plans/designs, and for how long does this responsibility last?
o: The IAPOA, from submission until the exhibition ends
The Owner, from the time he assumes responsibility for the plans/designs and for the duration of his responsibility; the insured amount is stated in the Conditions
The Competitors themselves, for the duration of the competition
The Professional Advisor, but only during Jury deliberations
n: The Owner shall insure the Competitors' plans/designs from the time when he assumes responsibility for them and for the duration of his responsibility. The amount of such insurance shall be stated in the Conditions. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 11.1)

q: What quality must the information supplied to competitors (social, economic, technical, geographical, topographical, etc.) have, and who may issue supplementary information for a second-stage competition?
o: It must be withheld until the second stage begins; the IAPOA issues supplements
It is optional and may be omitted for limited competitions
It must be specific and not open to misinterpretation; supplementary information approved by the Jury may be issued by the Owner to competitors proceeding to the second stage
It may be general and open to interpretation; the Professional Advisor issues supplements
n: Information supplied to competitors must be specific and not open to misinterpretation. Supplementary information and instructions approved by the Jury may be issued by the Owner to Competitors selected to proceed to the second stage of a two-stage competition. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 4.5)

q: Besides Jury members, who else is ineligible to compete in or assist a Competitor in the ADC?
o: Only foreign architects
Any member of the promoting body, associate, employee, or person concerned with the preparation or organization of the ADC
Any registered architect regardless of affiliation
Only architects who previously won a national ADC
n: No member of the promoting body, nor any associate or employee, nor any person concerned with the preparation or organization of the ADC, will be eligible to compete or assist a Competitor. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 7.2)

q: SCENARIO: A public exhibition of ADC entries, which included physical models submitted by several Competitors, closes on October 1. QUESTION: Under SPP Document 208, what happens to the drawings/plans that received no prize and were not purchased, and by when must the required models be returned to their Authors?
o: They shall be destroyed at the end of the exhibition unless the Conditions provide otherwise; models required to be returned must go back to the Authors, at the Owner's expense, within a month of the close of the exhibition — i.e., by November 1
They are transferred to the IAPOA archive; models are returned within one (1) week
They must all be preserved indefinitely by the Owner; models are returned within one (1) year
They are auctioned off to fund future competitions; models are never returned
n: All drawings and plans, other than those which received prizes or were purchased and retained by the Owner, shall be destroyed at the end of the public exhibition, unless the Conditions provide otherwise. Where models are required, these will be returned to the Author/s at the expense of the Owner within a month of the close of the public exhibition. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 13.1)
scenario: A public exhibition of ADC entries, which included physical models submitted by several Competitors, closes on October 1.

q: Which of the following correctly describes the Professional Advisor's role during Jury deliberations?
o: He assists the Jury and is present during its deliberations, but has no vote
He votes only on procedural, not substantive, matters
He presides over the Jury and casts the deciding vote in case of a tie
He is excluded from all Jury deliberations to preserve his neutrality
n: The Professional Advisor will assist the Jury and will be present during its deliberations but he will have no vote; his responsibilities are limited to the organization and conduct of the competition. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 5.1)

q: SCENARIO: An ADC's results are officially announced by the Owner on March 1. QUESTION: Under SPP Document 208, by what date at the latest must the Owner pay the prizes allotted by the Jury?
o: June 1 (three months after announcement)
March 8 (one week after announcement)
April 1 (one month after announcement)
There is no deadline; payment may be made at the Owner's convenience
n: The Owner undertakes to accept the decisions of the Jury and to pay the prizes allotted within one (1) month of the official announcement of the ADC results — i.e., by April 1 if announced March 1. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 8.3)
scenario: An ADC's results are officially announced by the Owner on March 1.

q: For a dispute not related to the adjudication process or the awarding of prizes, how must the matter be settled?
o: By an arbitration process approved by the IAPOA, without initial recourse to any form of litigation
By a private settlement between the Owner and the Professional Advisor
By immediate recourse to litigation
By a re-vote of the original Jury
n: In the event of a dispute not related to the adjudication process or awarding of the prizes, the matter shall be settled by an arbitration process approved by the IAPOA, and without initial recourse to any form of litigation. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 14.3)

q: Who appoints the Jurors for an ADC, and what role does the IAPOA play in this process?
o: The Jurors are appointed solely by the IAPOA without Owner involvement
The Jurors are elected by the registered Competitors
The Jurors are appointed by the Owner and approved by the IAPOA, which assists the Owner in the selection of Jury members
The Jurors are appointed by the Professional Advisor and ratified by the Competition Secretariat
n: The Jurors are appointed by the Owner and approved by the IAPOA, which shall assist the Owner in the selection of the Jury members. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 6.2)

q: What must the Conditions state regarding the Owner's use of the winning plan/design, and what legal provisions govern this?
o: The Owner may freely combine portions of any entries into a new design without consent

The Conditions shall state the use to which the Owner will put the winning scheme; ADC-generated plans/designs may not be used or altered except by agreement with the author, per Secs. 20(4) and 33 of R.A. No. 9266 and R.A. No. 8293
The winning design automatically becomes public domain upon award
Only the IAPOA may authorize use of the winning design
n: The Conditions shall state the use to which the Owner will put the winning plan/design; ADC-generated plans/designs may not be used or altered in any way except by agreement with the author. The Owner is not free to pick out portions of entries to compose another design — this is covered by ownership and copyright provisions under Secs. 20(4) and 33 of R.A. No. 9266 (Architecture Act of 2004) and R.A. No. 8293 (IP Code) and their IRRs. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 8.6)

q: Which government statutes are specifically cited in SPP Document 208 as the legal basis for copyright and ownership protections over ADC-generated designs?
o: R.A. No. 9285 (Alternative Dispute Resolution Act) only
Presidential Decree No. 1096 (National Building Code)
R.A. No. 9266 (The Architecture Act of 2004) and R.A. No. 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines), and their respective IRRs
R.A. No. 386 (The Civil Code of the Philippines) only
n: Secs. 8.6 and 9.4 cite R.A. No. 9266 (The Architecture Act of 2004, Secs. 20(4) and 33) and R.A. No. 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines), and their respective IRRs, as the basis for ownership and copyright protection of ADC-generated plans/designs. (R.A. No. 9285 is instead cited as the basis for the ADR modes in Sec. 14.) (Source: SPP Document 208, Secs. 8.6 and 9.4)

q: What is required to ensure correct conduct of the competition regarding representation on the Jury?
o: All Jurors must be non-architects to ensure impartiality
At least one of the Architect-Jurors shall represent the IAPOA
The Professional Advisor must be a voting Juror
The Owner must chair the Jury
n: To ensure correct conduct of the competition, at least one of the Architect-Jurors shall represent the IAPOA. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 6.4)

q: In an Ideas Competition, if the Owner decides to use all or part of the winning scheme, what must occur?
o: The Owner should do so with the collaboration of the Author, on terms acceptable to the Author
The Owner may proceed unilaterally since ideas are not protected
The Owner must pay a penalty to the IAPOA
The Owner must hold a second competition to select an executing architect
n: In an Ideas Competition, if the Owner decides to make use of all or part of the winning scheme, he should do so with the collaboration of the Author; the terms of collaboration must be acceptable to the latter. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 8.9)

q: What does the term "SPP on ADC" refer to in SPP Document 208?
o: The Jury's rulebook for scoring entries
The Philippine Standard of Professional Practice (SPP) on Architectural Design Competitions
The IAPOA's annual competition calendar
The Owner's internal competition guidelines
n: "SPP on ADC" refers to the Philippine Standard of Professional Practice (SPP) on Architectural Design Competitions (ADC) itself. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 2.8)

q: When must each Juror see the Conditions of the ADC?
o: Only after the entries are submitted
Before the Conditions are made available to Competitors
Only if the Juror requests to see them
At the same time as the Competitors, for fairness
n: Each Juror shall see the Conditions before they are made available to Competitors. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 6.7)

q: As a general rule, how many executions does the Owner's right to use the ADC-generated plan/design cover, and can this be altered?
o: Exactly two (2) executions — one for each competition stage
Unlimited executions, unless the Conditions state otherwise
One (1) execution only, as a general rule; however, the Conditions may provide for repetitive work and specify the terms thereof
Zero executions until a separate licensing agreement is signed
n: As a general rule, the Owner's right to use the ADC-generated plan/design covers one (1) execution only. However, the Conditions may provide for repetitive work and specify the terms thereof. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 9.3)

q: Under SPP Document 208, who issues the Notice of a National Architectural Design Competition, and what must such an announcement state?
o: The Owner and/or the IAPOA ADC Committee Secretariat; it must state where and how ADC documents may be obtained and that the Conditions received IAPOA approval
The Competition Secretariat only, published exclusively in the Official Gazette
The Professional Advisor alone; it must list all Jurors by name
Only the Jury; it need not mention IAPOA approval
n: Notice of a National ADC is issued by the Owner and/or the IAPOA ADC Committee Secretariat, with a request for publication in technical journals or other media; the announcement must state where and how ADC documents may be obtained and that the Conditions have received the requisite IAPOA approval. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 3.2)

q: What must the Jury do with drawings, photographs, models, or other documents not required under the regulations, before examining a Competitor's entry?
o: Score them as bonus material
Exclude them before examining the entry
Disqualify the entire entry automatically
Forward them to the Owner for separate review
n: Any drawings, photographs, models or other documents not required under the regulations shall be excluded by the Jury before it examines a Competitor's entry. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 6.10)

q: If the Owner requires a deposit as a condition for furnishing competition documentation, what happens to that deposit for Competitors who submit a bona fide plan/design?
o: It is returned to them, unless otherwise stated
It is forfeited to cover administrative costs
It is donated to the IAPOA ADC Committee
It is applied toward the registration fee for future competitions
n: The Owner shall issue to all Competitors the necessary documentation for preparing their plans/designs. Where furnishing such documentation is conditional on payment of a deposit, unless otherwise stated, such a deposit shall be returned to Competitors who submit a bona fide plan/design. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 10.2)

q: Under Sec. 4.3, the conditions for a National ADC (single or two-stage, open or limited) must clearly state all of the following EXCEPT:
o: The purpose of the ADC and the intentions of the Owner
The personal contact numbers of each Jury member
All the requirements which Competitors must meet
The nature of the problem to be solved
n: Sec. 4.3 requires the Conditions to clearly state the purpose of the ADC and intentions of the Owner, the nature of the problem to be solved, and all requirements competitors must meet — not personal contact details of Jurors. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 4.3.1-4.3.3)

q: Who bears the fees and travel/subsistence expenses of the Jury members?
o: The Professional Advisor
The Jury members themselves
The Owner
The IAPOA ADC Committee
n: The fees and travel and subsistence expenses of the Jury members shall be paid by the Owner. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 6.13)

q: SCENARIO: Following the Jury's decision on an ADC, the Owner opens a public exhibition of the entries, including those the Jury disqualified. QUESTION: As a general rule, for how long must this exhibition run, and what must accompany it?
o: Exactly thirty (30) days, with admission fees waived only for architects
No minimum duration is specified; it is left entirely to the Owner's discretion
At least one (1) week, together with the names of the disqualified Competitors
At least two (2) weeks, together with a copy of the signed report of the Jury, and it must be open to the public free of charge
n: All designs, including those disqualified by the Jury, shall be exhibited, as a general rule, for at least two (2) weeks, together with a copy of the signed report of the Jury. The exhibition shall be open to the public free of charge. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 12.1)
scenario: Following the Jury's decision on an ADC, the Owner opens a public exhibition of the entries, including those the Jury disqualified.

q: What must the Conditions state regarding documents, plans, or models required from competitors, and what applies when a cost estimate is required?
o: Only the deadline for submission; cost estimates are never required
The Professional Advisor decides format on a case-by-case basis after submission
Only the Jury may decide the format after entries are received
The number, nature, scale and dimensions of documents/plans/models required and terms of acceptance; where a cost estimate is required, a standard form of presentation must be prescribed
n: The Conditions shall state the number, nature, scale and dimensions of the documents, plans or models required and the terms of acceptance of such documents or models; where an estimate of cost is required, the Conditions must prescribe a standard form of presentation. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 4.6)

q: What must the Conditions state regarding prizes, and to what should the prizes awarded be related?
o: Only the first-prize amount; other prizes are optional
The prizes need not be disclosed until after judging
Only the total budget of the project, with prize amounts left to Jury discretion
The amount and number of prizes; these must be related to the size and complexity of the project, the amount of work involved, and the expense incurred by Competitors
n: The Conditions must state the amount and number of prizes. The prizes awarded must be related to the size and complexity of the project, the amount of work involved, and the expense incurred by Competitors. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 8.1)

q: What must be included in the ADC Conditions to address the possibility of disputes, and what legal framework governs these modes?
o: A waiver of all legal remedies for competitors
Provisions for conciliation, mediation and arbitration (ADR modes under R.A. No. 9285), which must precede any form of litigation
Nothing; disputes are handled solely through the courts
A mandatory arbitration clause naming the Owner as sole arbiter
n: Since no regulations, however well drawn up, can preclude the possibility of dispute, provisions for conciliation, mediation and arbitration — i.e., ADR modes under R.A. No. 9285 — must be included in the ADC Conditions and must precede any form of litigation. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 14.1)

q: Besides preparing the Conditions, which of the following is a specific function of the Professional Advisor under SPP Document 208?
o: Judging the technical merit of each design entry
Supervising receipt of Competitors' questions, dispatching replies to all Competitors, receiving competition entries, and safeguarding anonymity of Competitors at all times
Awarding prizes and honoraria directly to winning Competitors
Approving the Jury's final report for submission to IAPOA
n: The Professional Advisor's function includes ensuring the ADC timetable is adhered to, supervising receipt of Competitors' questions, dispatch of replies to all Competitors, receipt of competition entries, and safeguarding the anonymity of Competitors at all times. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 5.1)

q: In a limited ADC by invitation, what must each participant receive in addition to the prizes awarded?
o: A guaranteed commission on a future project
A certificate of participation only
An honorarium
Reimbursement of travel expenses only
n: Each participant in a limited ADC by invitation shall receive an honorarium in addition to the prizes awarded. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 8.4)

q: Who shares the expenses resulting from any conciliation, mediation, or arbitration procedure under an ADC dispute?
o: The IAPOA alone
The Jury members personally
The two (2) interested parties to the ADR proceeding, shared between them
The Owner alone
n: The expenses resulting from any conciliation, mediation or arbitration procedure shall be shared by the two (2) interested parties to the ADR proceeding. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 14.4)

q: SCENARIO: An Owner convening an ADC decides to appoint the maximum allowable number of Jurors under SPP Document 208. QUESTION: What is that maximum number, and how many of them must, at minimum, be Architects?
o: Five (5) members; at least two (2) must be Architects
Seven (7) members; the majority — 4 out of 7 — must be Architects
Seven (7) members; only one (1) needs to be an Architect
Nine (9) members; at least five (5) must be Architects
n: The Jury shall be composed of the smallest reasonable number of persons, in any event an odd number not exceeding seven (7); the majority of them — i.e., 4 out of 7 — shall be Architects. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 6.3)
scenario: An Owner convening an ADC decides to appoint the maximum allowable number of Jurors permitted under SPP Document 208.

q: In a Project ADC, what obligation does the award of first prize to a plan/design place on the Owner, and what happens if the winning Competitor cannot satisfy the Jury of his ability to carry out the work?
o: The Owner may freely rebid the project to any other architect

The Owner is obligated to entrust the Author with the commission for the Project; if the winner cannot satisfy the Jury of his ability, the Jury may require him to collaborate with another Architect of his choice, approved by the Jury and Owner
The Owner has no obligation beyond paying the prize money
The winning Competitor forfeits the prize entirely
n: In Project ADCs, the award of first prize to a plan/design places the Owner under an obligation to entrust the Author with the commission for the Project. If the winning Competitor is unable to satisfy the Jury of his ability to carry out the work, the Jury may require him to collaborate with another Architect of his choice, duly approved by the Jury and Owner. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 8.7)

q: Across SPP Document 208, the IAPOA (through its ADC Committee) is shown approving or being involved in which of the following series of matters?
o: Only disputes that reach litigation
Only the final exhibition dates

The draft Conditions before announcement, the appointment of Jurors (jointly with the Owner), the Professional Advisor's appointment (through the NBD), a single-stage competition's move to a second stage, and settlement of disputes not related to adjudication or prizes
Only the amount of the registration fee
n: Throughout the document, the IAPOA (through its ADC Committee, or NBD for the Professional Advisor) is involved in approving the draft Conditions (Sec. 3.1), assisting in Jury selection (Sec. 6.2), approving the Professional Advisor's appointment (Sec. 5.1), approving a single-stage competition's move to a second stage (Sec. 6.9), and approving the arbitration process for disputes not related to adjudication or prizes (Sec. 14.3). (Source: SPP Document 208, Secs. 3.1, 5.1, 6.2, 6.9, 14.3)

q: What is the maximum number of Owner representatives that may be included in the Jury?
o: One (1)
None — the Owner may not have any representative on the Jury
Three (3), one for each stage
Two (2)
n: There should not be more than one (1) representative of the Owner included in the Jury. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 6.5)

q: Who retains the copyright of a submitted plan/design, and what is required before any alterations may be made?
o: The Owner retains copyright automatically upon submission
Copyright is jointly held by the Owner and Author from the outset
The Author retains the copyright of his work; no alterations may be made without his/her written consent
The IAPOA holds copyright in trust for the Jury
n: The Author of any plan/design shall retain the copyright of his work; no alterations may be made without his/her written consent. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 9.1)

q: Who appoints the IAPOA ADC Committee, and what is its role?
o: The Professional Advisor appoints it to draft the Conditions
The IAPOA National President appoints it to oversee all ADCs referred to the IAPOA
The Jury appoints it to handle disputes
The Owner appoints it to judge entries directly
n: The IAPOA ADC Committee is appointed by the IAPOA National President to oversee all architectural design competitions (ADCs) referred to the IAPOA. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 2.9)

q: How does the Jury take its decisions, and what happens once the competition awards are finalized?
o: By unanimous vote only; no report is required

By majority vote, with a separate vote on each plan/design submitted; the list of ADC awards and the Jury's report shall be signed by all Jurors before the Jury is dissolved, and a copy sent to the IAPOA
By the Professional Advisor's tie-breaking vote; the report stays confidential
By the Owner's final ratification of the Jury's recommendation
n: The decisions of the Jury shall be taken by a majority vote, with a separate vote on each competition plan/design submitted. The list of ADC awards, including the Jury's report to the Owner, shall be signed by all Jurors before the Jury is dissolved, and one copy of this document shall be sent to the IAPOA. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 6.8)

q: Unless otherwise stated in the Conditions, who retains the sole right of reproduction of any ADC design, and under what legal basis?
o: The Author, by virtue of sole copyright under Secs. 20(4) and 33 of R.A. No. 9266 (Architecture Act of 2004) and its IRR
The Owner, under the Civil Code provisions on ownership
The IAPOA, as custodian of all competition entries
The Professional Advisor, as custodian of the Conditions
n: In all cases, unless otherwise stated in the Conditions, the Author of any design shall retain the sole right of reproduction by virtue of sole copyright under Secs. 20(4) and 33 of R.A. No. 9266 (The Architecture Act of 2004) and its IRR. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 9.4)

q: An architect serving as Professional Advisor notices that a competitor's identity has become known to some Jurors before final judgment. What principle of SPP Document 208 has been compromised?
o: The rule limiting the Jury to seven members
The requirement that conditions be identical for all competitors
The anonymity of competitors, which must be maintained until final judgment
The rule on registration of competitors
n: It is essential that the anonymity of competitors be maintained until the final judgment of the competition; rigorous measures should be taken to ensure this principle is observed. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 4.1)
